Definition: from δάνος (a gift); probably akin to the base of G1325; a loan:--debt.
BiblicalUsage: The word appears once, in the parable of the unmerciful servant: the lord forgave his servant the debt, and the servant seized his fellow and demanded payment. The loan is the picture of what we owe God, and the forgiveness is the picture of what He gives.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the parable turns on this word: the debt we owe is unpayable, and the mercy we receive must be passed on.
